addition.item: Deleting an item (an article, category, contact or user) now deletes its files as well, unless another item still uses them.
Unused files are now cleaned up automatically: once a day, the first upload also deletes the files that no field names and that are older than the grace period.
A setting for how long unsaved uploads are kept before Delete unused files may remove them, 7 days by default. It was a fixed day.

fix.item: Downloads now work on pages served from Joomla's view cache (System Cache: Conservative) and from the System - Page Cache plugin. A button fetches a fresh download token when it is pressed, instead of sending the one the cached page was rendered with for another visitor.

security.item: Uploads and previews now require everything the item form asks before it offers the field: the field and its field group are published, the field is editable on the current side of the site, the editor's access levels include the field's, and the editor has Edit Custom Field Value on the field. Before, edit permission on the item was enough, so every registered user could upload to their own profile through a field meant for administrators only.
One session can have at most 50 uploads waiting for their item to be saved.

Files are now bound to the item they were uploaded for. A save keeps only the files the item already listed and the ones uploaded for it in the editor's session, so an editor can no longer attach another item's file, whose name is no secret, to an item they edit and offer it under that item's access rules. Save as Copy still takes over the files of the item it copies.

The content of an upload must now match its extension, so a web page or a script can no longer be stored as, for example, a PDF. File types an administrator adds to the allowed list are accepted without this check, and logged.

A file that was uploaded but not saved yet can only be previewed, or replaced and deleted, from the session that uploaded it for that item. Before, any editor could preview or delete any file that no item listed.

addition.item: First release of Pretty Protected Downloads: a custom field for articles that offers files for download without ever giving them a public URL.

Files are stored outside the web root, or inside it in a folder closed with .htaccess, and are only served after the article, category, field and field group access levels and the publishing dates have been checked.
Every download button carries a short-lived token bound to the visitor's session, so a file can only be fetched from a page the visitor was allowed to see.
Upload straight from the article form, with progress, a per-file button text, title, description, icon and button style.
Three display layouts, buttons, cards and list, each with an optional file type and size, and each overridable from the template.
Works on articles, categories, contacts and user profiles, and inside subform fields.
Allowed file types and a maximum file size; scripts, web pages and SVG images are always refused.
Visitors download the file under the name it was uploaded with.
A storage status on the plugin settings screen, and a button that deletes stored files no field uses any more.
